The explicit inverse DFT b_j=1+(1/m)Σ_{k∈A}ζ^(jk) is real and ≥1/m, and has coefficients m at zero, zero at designated frequencies and one elsewhere. Real DFT invertibility yields independent codimension |E| equations. Nonnegative column sums give the exact power norm and linear growth. Rank-one finite perturbation of the shift-plus-permutation block preserves Fredholm essential spectrum and index; approximate shift eigenvectors give the unit-circle approximate spectrum. The standalone finite checker passed 38474 supplementary tests; universal claims rest on the displayed proofs.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical one-way rank-one positive coupling from a finite periodic component to a unilateral shift on the standard KB Banach lattice l1. Its natural invariant—the peripheral point eigenvalue set—is classified for every conjugate-invariant subset of the fixed finite root group, with exact algebraic strata and codimensions. The single model provides arbitrarily small positive perturbations of a power-bounded isometry while the eigenvalue pattern changes arbitrarily and operator powers grow at an explicitly computable linear rate; thus it sharply explains the necessity of growth hypotheses for point-spectrum cyclicity in this setting. It is not only a single counterexample or a known subgroup-minus-one construction.
